title: The Ferry Without a Pilot
premise_public: During a brief power cut, a small ferry crossed a fast river and docked on time. Its engine was not running, no one was steering at the wheel, and the passengers treated the trip as ordinary.
solution_summary: It was a reaction ferry. A fixed cable constrained the boat's path across the river, while the operator had set its angle to the flowing water. The river current supplied the force that carried the ferry across, so it needed neither a running engine nor someone steering at a wheel during the crossing.

facts.text: A fixed cable guided the ferry's route across the river.
The ferry was set at an angle to the direction of flowing water.
The river current supplied the force that moved the ferry sideways across the river.
An operator arranged the ferry's angle before the crossing rather than steering at a wheel during it.
The crossing did not depend on electricity or engine power.

acceptable_solutions: The ferry was tethered to a cable and angled into the river current so the water pushed it across without an engine.
It was a reaction ferry using the flow of the river and a guide cable, not a pilot at the wheel.
The boat crossed using the river's current against its angled hull while a cable kept it on course.
hints: The power cut matters less if the crossing uses a different source of energy.
Think about how a fixed route and moving water might work together.
